question.:question/problem: Find the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{\left(x+5\right)}}{\sqrt{\left(y+4\right)}}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the general solution, we first separate the variables: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\sqrt{\left(x+5\right)}}{\sqrt{\left(y+4\right)}} \\ \sqrt{\left(y+4\right)}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\sqrt{\left(x+5\right)}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \sqrt{\left(y+4\right)}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int \sqrt{\left(x+5\right)}\,\text{d}x \\ \int \sqrt{\left(y+4\right)}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\cancel{\text{d}x}}\,\cancel{\text{d}x} & =\int \sqrt{\left(x+5\right)}\,\text{d}x \\ \int {\left(y+4\right)}^{1/2}\,\text{d}y & =\int {\left(x+5\right)}^{1/2}\,\text{d}x \\ \frac{2{\left(y+4\right)}^{3/2}}{3} & =\frac{2{\left(x+5\right)}^{3/2}}{3}+K \\ {\left(y+4\right)}^{3/2} & ={\left(x+5\right)}^{3/2}+C \\ \sqrt{{\left(y+4\right)}^{3}} & =\sqrt{{\left(x+5\right)}^{3}}+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=\frac{3K}{2}.$

Therefore, the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) is

$$
\sqrt{{\left(y+4\right)}^{3}}=\sqrt{{\left(x+5\right)}^{3}}+C.
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2x}{{e}^{\left(y+5\right)}}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the general solution, we first separate the variables: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{2x}{{e}^{\left(y+5\right)}} \\ {e}^{\left(y+5\right)}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =2x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {e}^{\left(y+5\right)}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int 2x\,\text{d}x \\ \int {e}^{\left(y+5\right)}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\cancel{\text{d}x}}\,\cancel{\text{d}x} & =\int 2x\,\text{d}x \\ \int {e}^{\left(y+5\right)}\,\text{d}y & =\int 2x\,\text{d}x \\ {e}^{\left(y+5\right)} & ={x}^{2}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) is

$$
{e}^{\left(y+5\right)}={x}^{2}+C.
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\sqrt{1-{\left(y-2\right)}^{2}}\,$ for $\,|\left(y-2\right)|<1.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the general solution, we first separate the variables: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\sqrt{1-{\left(y-2\right)}^{2}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{\left(y-2\right)}^{2}}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{\left(y-2\right)}^{2}}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int \,\text{d}x \\ \int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{\left(y-2\right)}^{2}}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\cancel{\text{d}x}}\,\cancel{\text{d}x} & =\int \,\text{d}x \\ \int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{\left(y-2\right)}^{2}}}\,\text{d}y & =\int \text{d}x \\ \operatorname{arcsin}⁡\left(y-2\right) & =x+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) is

$$
\operatorname{arcsin}⁡\left(y-2\right)=x+C.
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the general solution to the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=2{e}^{-y}(x-1).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the general solution, we first separate the variables: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =2{e}^{-y}(x-1) \\ {e}^{y}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =2(x-1)\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {e}^{y}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\text{d}x & =\int 2(x-1)\,\text{d}x \\ \int {e}^{y}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\cancel{\text{d}x}}\,\cancel{\text{d}x} & =\int 2x\,\text{d}x-\int 2\,\text{d}x \\ {e}^{y} & ={x}^{2}-2x+C\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) is

$$
{e}^{y}={x}^{2}-2x+C.
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the general solution to the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{y}}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the general solution, we first separate the variables: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{y}} \\ \sqrt{y}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\sqrt{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \sqrt{y}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int \sqrt{x}\,\text{d}x \\ \int \sqrt{y}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\cancel{\text{d}x}}\,\cancel{\text{d}x} & =\int \sqrt{x}\,\text{d}x \\ \int {y}^{1/2}\,\text{d}y & =\int {x}^{1/2}\,\text{d}x \\ \frac{2{y}^{3/2}}{3} & =\frac{2{x}^{3/2}}{3}+K \\ {y}^{3/2} & ={x}^{3/2}+C \\ \sqrt{{y}^{3}} & =\sqrt{{x}^{3}}+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=\frac{3K}{2}.$

Therefore, the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) is

$$
\sqrt{{y}^{3}}=\sqrt{{x}^{3}}+C.
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the general solution to the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{3{x}^{2}}{\operatorname{cos}⁡y}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{3{x}^{2}}{\operatorname{cos}⁡y} \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡y\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =3{x}^{2}\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \operatorname{cos}⁡y\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int 3{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\ \int \operatorname{cos}⁡y\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\cancel{\text{d}x}}\,\cancel{\text{d}x} & =\int 3{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\ \int \operatorname{cos}⁡y\,\text{d}y & =\int 3{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡y & ={x}^{3}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) is

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡y={x}^{3}+C.

question.:question/problem: Find the general solution to the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{sec}⁡y\operatorname{tan}⁡y}$ for $x\ne 0$ and $-\frac{\pi }{2}<y<\frac{\pi }{2}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the general solution, we first separate the variables: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{x\operatorname{sec}⁡y\operatorname{tan}⁡y} \\ \operatorname{sec}⁡y\operatorname{tan}⁡y\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \operatorname{sec}⁡y\operatorname{tan}⁡y\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\ \int \operatorname{sec}⁡y\operatorname{tan}⁡y\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\cancel{\text{d}x}}\,\cancel{\text{d}x} & =\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\ \int \operatorname{sec}⁡y\operatorname{tan}⁡y\,\text{d}y & =\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\ \operatorname{sec}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+C\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) is

$$
\operatorname{sec}⁡y=\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+C.
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the general solution to the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=y\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ for $y\ne 0.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the general solution, we first separate the variables: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =y\operatorname{sin}⁡x \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int \operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\ \int \frac{1}{y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\cancel{\text{d}x}}\,\cancel{\text{d}x} & =\int \operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\ \int \frac{1}{y}\,\text{d}y & =\int \operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡|y| & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡x+C\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) is

$$
\operatorname{ln}⁡|y|=-\operatorname{cos}⁡x+C
$$
